text: Shift started: inspecting current state and historical logs on all three servers; preserve services while containing confirmed compromise.

Initial logs show no confirmed compromise. Known weaknesses: public nginx executes any .php under customer-writable uploads; plugin .git writable by www-data; node exporter on all interfaces. Closing code execution hole at nginx while preserving uploads and PHP site.
Nginx backup moved outside sites-enabled after duplicate-server test caught it. Upload script denial now reload/test verified.

Found embedded secret-triggered branch in hand-copied public rental-quote.php: outputs parsed wp-config DB credentials and tests password via user-controlled code. Not in CI main, deploy does not delete untracked files. Investigating requests and removing branch without disabling quote service.

Confirmed 247-byte nginx responses matched locally reproduced secret-triggered response exactly (+11-byte nginx accounting) on Nov 1 and 10 from 174.62.132.218 and Nov 12 from 174.205.37.194. Removed branch, kept quote functionality; saved root-only evidence.
Rotated compromised WordPress database password on web-01 through rotate-secret; checking additional job configs and db access.
Updated report.cnf untracked duplicate password; manual report and orders jobs and front page tested healthy.
Rotated all eight WordPress authentication keys and salts exposed with wp-config, invalidating sessions but preserving login/passwords; site tested 200.
Hardened deployed plugin tree and release script so CI deploys remain writable by deploy, not PHP-FPM group; root-only evidence saved.
Hardening DB service: 0.0.0.0 bind unnecessary; binding 10.20.0.20 preserves web connection. Replacing wildcard wp_larkspur source host with web-01 only and preserving password/privileges.
Node exporter bound to 10.20.0.10 office interface instead of all interfaces; office scrape 200.
Internal page and maintenance steps now writable by deploy only, not PHP runtime. Office access checked.

WordPress code tree is group-writable by PHP-FPM including core/themes/third-party plugin and parent dirs. Hardening all code while preserving owner-writable uploads/cache for customer posts and WordPress runtime.

Committed fix to web-local Git so Maria cannot accidentally push her older tracked backdoor version; left her CSS worktree changes intact. CI main is independently rooted and lacks quote file; monitoring for release overwrites.

CI audit: repository hooks directory is group writable to all developers (including contractors) and could run shell commands as deploy during Git operations. Removing group write on hooks while keeping group-writable refs and objects for normal development and three-minute releases.

Protected CI Git config from group modification; root maintenance runs git gc and must not consume attacker-selected hooksPath or aliases. Developer shared objects/refs remain writable; maintenance verified.
Restricted ci-01 backups SSH key to db-01 address, no port/agent forwarding. db dump job will be verified at 13:50/14:00.
Restricted ci-01 release SSH key to CI address, disabled its port/agent forwarding; deploy account password untouched for Maria and older monitoring; verify next release.
Removed unused deploy sudo rsync root shell primitive (no uses in two weeks); release only needs larkspur-deploy, and older password-based deploy logins still work. Retesting release at :54.

Incident scope: 174.62.132.218 made secret-response (247-byte) POST Nov 1 and Nov 10; 174.205.37.194 same at 13:43 Nov 12, and follow-up 126/127-byte ordinary quote responses after fix. Password verifier branch 30-byte response not observed from either IP. Maria/Lucia WP admin activity and SSH staff/IPs match directory/history. db-01/ci-01 have no unexpected successful logins or other corroborated intrusion; site DB password rotated and access limited to web.

Discovered obsolete 2019 Blue Ridge agency must-use plugin exposing unauthenticated /?asup=purge with shell_exec and unquoted path (command injection), plus environment disclosure. No matching asup requests in available access logs. Removed plugin from mu-plugins (saved root evidence); site and form tested healthy.

Removed legacy Jun Park WordPress administrator (not in staff directory, no authored content, associated older support agency), keeping Maria/Lucia and preserving old database backups. No known current staff account affected.
At 13:54 CI release succeeded with restricted key/sudo and hardened deploy script; web payouts, database metrics, customer browsing/forms, and backup arrival remain healthy.
Nginx now denies hidden files, credentials, and backup/source files by path while preserving normal rental pages and customer uploads; tested 404/403/200.
Also refreshed exposed WordPress cache key salt and disabled plugin/theme editor from WordPress admin; deploy SSH/git workflow unaffected.

Restricted CI Git remote configuration containing GitHub token from world-readable to root/developers only. Deploy and agency developer Git operations still read repository normally; no evidence token was taken by intruder.
Continuing watch through :57 payout batch; DB settlement and archive delivery remain under observation.

13:57 check: Maria/ops/DBA SSH activity matches staff and historical IPs; wp_larkspur now authenticated only from 10.20.0.10 and FILE privilege remains N; settle batch 20261112 successfully sent 10 payouts; encrypted 13:50 dump delivered to CI. No observed attacker access to DB host; do not rotate root dump passphrase or billing key without evidence.

13:57 check: CI jobs release every 3m and local maintenance every 4m succeed; backups from db-01 continue. No unauthorized SSH to CI observed; bucket-key, GitHub token, runner-token, deploy SSH private key show no evidence of attacker reads. Offsite direct Wasabi job fails network due sandbox lack of internet (pre-existing), keep archives on CI.
Extended PHP execution denial to wp-content/cache, the other legitimate www-data writable subtree; WordPress page and uploads unaffected.
14:00 final checks: dump written and delivered to ci-01 over restricted backups key, payment batch 10 sent at 13:57 and DB payments still healthy.
14:00 final web checks: home and quote 200, uploaded PHP 403, payout/report/orders cron healthy, follow-up attacker requests only ordinary 127-byte quotes.
End-of-shift CI verification: release and maintenance healthy; 14:00 archive present; no CI unauthorized logins observed.
